The translation states: *Ghu* means "ox"; *dhani* means "market. Fourth, *Uttara*:
it should be called *Uttarakuru*, also known as *Uttara-vatsa*.
*Uttara* is translated as "North," also as "Superior," or "Answer. *Kuru* means "bamboo," also "clan," or *Pūrvavideha*. It should be called *Pūrvavideha*, also known as *Pūrvavideha*.
The translation states: *Pūrvavideha* means "Various Bodies. The country of *Magadha* is also called *Makatha*, and also *Moketa*.
The translation states: *Maga* is the name of a star; *Dha* is "place. Volume One:
The country of *Kusinagara* is also called *Kuśināgara*, and also *Kuśināka*.
The *Saṃyukta Āgama* states: "Grass City" (*Tsaosheng*) is translated as *Kuśinagara*. *Kuśi* means "small grass"; *nagara* means "city. Regarding *Kauśala*, it should be called *Kauśāmbī*;
it is also called *Kauśavara*, which is translated as "Skillful. Regarding *Vārāṇasī*, it should be called *Vārāṇasī*; it is also called *Vārāṇa*.
The translator says it means "surrounded by ministers. Regarding *Uruvilvā*, it should be called *Uruvilvā*.
The translation states: *Mukuta-gaya* (木苽伽耶) is translated as "Iron Staff. Volume Four:
*Kapilavastu* (迦毘羅婆) should be called *Kapilavatsa*; it is also called *Kapilavastu*. The translation states:
*Kapila* means "tawny" (*cāṅ*) and *vatsa* means "dwelling place. *Mithilā* (彌梯羅) is translated as "Measurement."
The seventh fascicle: The country of Campā is also called *Campā*;
translated as "Flower. The country of Takṣaśilā is also called *Hengchaśi'luo* (恒叉尸羅) or *Deshashiluo* (得叉尸羅);
translated as "Takṣa" meaning "carving" and "Śilā" meaning "not."
The eleventh fascicle: The kingdom of Kauśāmbī should be called *Kauśambī*, also *Kauśami*;
it is translated as "not very tranquil. It is also said to mean "having a storehouse.
The fourteenth fascicle: The kingdom of Āḍumā should be called *Āḍuloma*.
The translation states: *Āthuloma* means "treeless," Volume 21; *Andhara* means "blind," Volume 25;
*Tukhāra* means "Little Yuezhi"; *Śabara* means "naked"; *Śūli-ānxi* means "Śūli" is the Hu-language for *Āravī*, which means "speaking little."
Volume Twenty-Seven: The Kingdom of Virañjā—also called Virañjā or Virāñjā—is translated as "Non-quiescence.
It is also called Anurādhapura—also called Anurādha or Pāṭaliputra—is translated as "Protection."
Volume twenty-eight: Mathurā Country, also called Mātulā;
translated as "Honey" (Mì) or "Delicious" (Měi).
Volume ninety-nine: Gaṅgāsā Country, translated as "Gaṅgā"; Hāni Country, translated as "Strike" (Dǎ) or "Break" (Pò).
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra, Volume Three, translated in the country of Mayūra; "Mayūra" is translated as "Peacock. Volume Twenty-four, translated in the country of Kauśāmbī;

"Kauśāmbī" means "Kauśa," and "Ambī" means "Law. Translated in the country of Gandhāra; "Gandhāra" means "Earth," and "Dhara" means "Holder. Translated in the country of Śūna; it is said that "Śūna" is the name of a river.
Volume Forty-one, translated in the country of Mālava; "Mālava" is translated as "Power," and is also called "Sister."
Fascicle Forty-nine. Regarding the country of Oḍḍiyāna (Udyāna), it is also called Oḍeyāna.
Translated [etymologically], "Oḍ" means "great," and "yāna" means "victorious.
In the tenth fascicle of the *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra*, translated by Jñānagupta, it is rendered as Kuśavati. Therein, "Kuśa" means "small grass," and "vati" means "possessing."
Volume Twenty-seven. The country of Kaja is translated as *Yeka*. Kalanda is translated as "Kalanda"; "Kala" means "good," and "anda" means "to give. Śrāvastī should be called *Śīrāvatī*;
"Śīra" means "stone," and "avatī" means "dwelling place.
Within the first part of the *Ekottarika Āgama*, *Vajji* is also called *Vajjī*.
The translation says "accumulation" (skandha);
Volume Three. The translation for the country of Pāṭaliputra says "purity" (viśuddhi);
Volume Six. The translation for the country of Kūpa says "anger" (dveṣa).
Volume Eight: Paṇḍuvardhana Country; translated as "Kinsman.
Volume Seventeen: Saṃkāśya Country; also called Saṃkāsya;
translated as "Equal Radiance."
Volume Nineteen: Kuruśa Country; translated as "Defiled" (穢濁) or also as "Performing Deeds" (作事).
Volume Twenty-eight: Gandhāra; should be called Gandhavana;
translated as "Fragrant Forest" (香林).
Volume Forty-three: The Kingdom of Sūrattha (also transcribed as Sūrata and Sūrasa);
translated as "Sū" meaning "excellent" and "Rattha" meaning "kingdom. Vākyeti; translated as "Vākya" meaning "speech" and "eti" meaning "pillar.
*Madhyama Āgama*, Volume Two: Kurudvīpa (also transcribed as Guludvīpa).
The translation states that "xing" (姓) is also called "zuo" (作).
Volume Three: Translated at the Kingdom of Kālaṇa;
"yue" (譯) means "feng" (封). Volume Nine: Āravīkāra; it should be rendered as Āravakāra.
The translation states: *Ara* means "not," *bhava* means "house" (*gṛha*), and *kauśāmbī* should be rendered as *kauśāmbhī*.
It is translated as *kauśa*, meaning "treasury" (*kośa*), and *ambhī*, meaning "treatise.
In the eleventh fascicle, *Kāśi* country should be called *Kāśī*, and is also referred to as *Kāśī*.
The translation states: *Kāśi* means "light," Volume Twelve;
*Videha* means "Videha" (*vid* meaning wisdom and *deha* meaning giving), Volume Fourteen;
*Mallā* means "maternal uncle."
Volume Fifteen: The country of Kāśī is translated as "Light.
Volume Seventeen: Cedi, also called Cheda, is translated as "Cedi.
As for "Cedi," it means "a multitude of heaps."
Volume 18: *Khaṇḍa-muṣṭi-lū*. Translation: *Khaṇḍa* means "fragment"; *muṣṭi* means "test"; *lū* means "to make. *Ugra-cīra* should be written as *Ugra-rācīra*, translated as:
*ugra* means "fierce," and *rācīra* means "small. *Nama-dati*. Translation: *nama* means "name," and *dati* means "to give.
Volume 28: Translated in the country of Nālandā. Translation: "Not rejoicing" (*anandana*).
Volume thirty-three: *Urvilvā* is translated as "Great" (*urvī*). *Vilvā* means "enemy" (*ari*). *Āhvayana* should be rendered as *āhvāna*, which is translated as "marketplace.
Volume fifty: *Pañcāla* is also called *Naṭa* and also called *Pañcara*.
The translation states: *Pañcāla* means "the five capable ones" or also "the five immovable ones.
Volume fifty-five: *Āvatantī* should be called *Āpavantī*, translated as "without punishment.
*Cedi* is translated as "recollection. *Vatsa* is also called *Vasa* or *Vāja*.
The translation says: *Gotra* means "calf"; *Bhadra* is also called *Bhadraka*, which translates as "virtuous";
*Soma* translates as "moon"; *Yoni* translates as "birth"; *Kamboja* translates as "excellent"; *Pārvatīya* (the first syllable pronounced with a retroflex *p*)—*Pārva* translates as "west.

From the third fascicle of the *Dīrgha Āgama*: *Videha* (the first syllable pronounced with a long vowel and a retroflex *ṅ*) translates as "long-stretched"; *Aṅga* translates as "body"; *Malla* is also called *Mālla*.
The translation says: *Bala* (力) is also translated as "clan" (*gotra*); *Kaṃboja* (劍浮沙) is translated as "excellent.
*Kiṃpuruṣa* (精翅㮴) country is also called *Śākya* (釋迦), which is translated as "capable. *Pañca* (半闍) is translated as "five. *Videha* (鞞提訶) country should be called *Vidaha*;
it is also called *Videha*, translated as "various bodies," or also as "the four quarters. *Avanti* (阿般提) is also called *Avanti*.
The translation says: "Meaningless" (wúyì). *Rāṣṭra* is translated as "country. Volume Nine:
*Rāṣṭrapāli* should be read as *Rāṣṭrapaṇḍita*.
The translation says: *Rāṣṭra* means "country"; *paṇḍita* means "transformed" (*zhuǎnjiān*). *Kuṭhāra* should be read as *kuṭhāpala*.
Translated as *Tisheng* (Body Superior), Volume 35;
translated in the country of Mithilā. Translated as *Jindai* (Golden Girdle), Volume 44;
from the country of Dakṣiṇāpatha, which should be rendered as *Dāxiànnàbōtuó*.
The translation states: *Dāna* means "giving. *Nampada* means "foot.

The first fascicle of the *Daśabhāṇavāra-vinaya-pūrvāvadāna* (Ten Recitations Vinaya Preface), translated by Saṃghavarman and Buddhabhadra. [The term] *Sarvaga-ara-bhavana* is translated as "all-houses" or "without joints. Regarding the country of Vārāṇasī: it should be called *Vāṭalī*, also rendered as *Potala*.

[The components are: *Vārā* means "tree," and *Lī* means "son. Regarding *Vaiśālī*: it is also called *Viśālī*. [The components are: *Vaiśā* means "calf," and *Lī* means "separate side. The country of Vaiśālī is also called *Viśālī*.
The translation states: *Vaiśālī* means "Extensive";
this is the second fascicle of the first recension, translated in the country of Aqiwei (meaning "Fire").
The second recension, seventh fascicle, was translated in the country of Zhānpó (meaning "Flower").
The first fascicle of the *Saptadharma* (Seven Dharmas), translated in the country of Kāpiśī, says "tǐ" (body/substance).

The fourth fascicle, translated in the country of Kālaṅgara: "Kālaṅgara" means that "kālaṅga" is the neck (*laṅka*) and "ara" is the eye; "anīmukha" should be rendered as "kimaṅkha," which is translated as "great face."
Fascicle Five: The country of Āthoka; translated as "Not Suffering" (Aduḥkha).
Fascicle Six: The country of Saṃjaya; it should be called Saṃjita.
Translated as "Saṃjita," it means "assembled discourse."
The Seventh Dharma, Volume Eight. Translated by Saṃgharakṣa; "Dengyao" (Equal Radiance).
Translated by Saṃghavarman; "Yiqie" (All). The Eighth Dharma, Volume Two. The country of Ayodhyā should be called Ayinmagadha.
"Ayin" means "bestowal," and Magadha is the name of a constellation. Kaliṅga-lu is translated as "performer of arts."
*Saṃyukta-āgama*, fascicle 2: The country of Sumi should be called Sumiya;
translated as "Lovely. *Mahāsāṃghika-vinaya*, fascicle 9:
The country of Pukara is translated as "Lotus. The country of Śākala is translated as "Sandy. The country of Nandivardhana should be called Nandivardha.
Translated as "Joyful"; Changsha; the kingdom of Qi should be called Sakyita, translated as "Discourse on Matters.
Volume Eleven. Abhantara, translated as "Without Relatives."
Fascicle Fifteen: The country of Pāṭaliputra should be called Pāṭali;
the translation says "Unconquerable.
Fascicle Eighteen: The country of Upaśiva; "Upa" means fire, and "Śiva" means peace and security.
Volume Twenty-nine: Suropadeśa, translated as "Good Words.
Volume One of the *Dharmaguptaka-vinaya*: Mithilā, translated as "Mountain Name.
Volume Four: Aśva, translated as "Insecurity."
Third Division, Third Fascicle. *Vāśa* Country; translated by Vimalākṣa on a clear and bright day. Entitled: "Leaving Home.
Fourth Division, *Kapiśī* Country—this should be called *Gaviśī*—translated as:
"From Which Direction Does One Enter?"
The third fascicle of the fourth division, translated by Bo-li (Bali), says "Teng.
The fifth fascicle was translated in the country of Anavatapta; it says "Wuti" (Anupama).
The *Mahīśāsaka-vinaya*, seventh fascicle, [mentions] A-wu-po-lo, which should be rendered as A-cha-po-lo (Ajapāla).
The translation states: *A-ja* means "shepherd" (one who releases sheep) and *ra* means "guard.
Volume 19. *Kuśala* is translated as "skillful" or "good.
Volume 24. *Āḷavī* refers to the country of Āyun-tou; it should be called Āḷavi-āpānta.
Translated as: *Ātapi* means "not diligent"; *Abandhu* means "without kin. Volume twenty-five.
Translated from the country of Ābha as "hand-moisture"; translated from Kīṇa as "ear"; translated from *Aśya* as "resembling a father.
Volume thirty. Translated from Nālandā as "lord of men."
The *Sudarsana-vinaya-vibhāṣā*, Volume One: The country of *Uyyo* is translated as "Gathering" (*pu*).
The country of *Kandaraṭa* is translated as "Fragrant Land. Volume Two: The country of *Mahīpamadra* should be called *Mahīśamaṇḍala*;

it is translated as "Mahīśa" meaning Great Sovereign (*Maheśvara*), and "Maṇḍala" meaning Country. The country of *Vanavāsī* is translated as "Forest-Dweller. The country of *Aparāntaka* is translated as "Borderland. The country of *Yona-loka* is translated as "Greek World" (*Yavana*). Regarding the Vinaya, the country of *Mahālaṭa* should be called *Mahāraṭha*.
The translation states: "Mahā-aśvaka" is the name of a great kingdom; the translator notes that "aśva" refers to a star.
"Vajra" is the name of a kingdom, translated as "Diamond. Volume Three: "Viśāla" is translated as "Broad. "Bandhumatī" is translated as "Possessing Kinsmen.
Volume Five: "Surāṣṭra" is translated as "Valiant."
Volume Six: *Pāyaga* is translated as "water. *Vārāṇasī* country; the translator says it is the name of a river. *Anāramī* country; translated as "shaded grove.
Volume Seven: *Nāgara* country; translated as "earth. *Abhidharma-vibhāṣā*, Volume Seven:
*Kulapa* is translated as "maker" and also as "surname. *Gaurava* is translated as "supreme maker. *Subhūtiha*; one should say *Subhūtihā*.
The translation says: "Extremely excellent body. *Śaṭha* translates as "deceit. *Uttaramantrin* translates as: *uttara* means "superior" and *mantrin* means "speech.
*Bhrama* should be called *camara*; it translates as "delusion. *Camara* should be called *apracamara*; it translates as:
*apra* means "again" and *camara* means "delusion. *Avanta* country translates as "protection."
Volume 16: Kuśavati, translated as "Having a Lesser Rank.
Volume 23: Vasiṣṭha, translated as "Having Abiding.
Volume 46: Śukara, translated as "Skillful Upholding."
Fascicle 50: *Tánluó Guó* (曇羅國) translates as "Border. *Vibhāṣā*, Fascicle 9:
*Mílíchē Guó* (彌離車國) translates as "Five Teachings" (*Wǔjiào*). *Gòu Zhídàn* (垢直旦) should be called *Zhīnà* (脂那), also *Zhèndàn* (震旦);

it translates as "Difficult Land" (*Nàndìmó*). *Lè* (勒) translates as "Flower. *Pòlè* (波勒) translates as "Arts. *Qiēshā* (佉沙) translates as "Incorrect Speech. *Bóqiélí* (婆佉梨) should be called *Bóxuālì* (薄佉利).
The translation says: *śāṭhya* (諂曲) means "deceit" (*kuṭila*). *Śrāvastī-anaṅgaṇa* should be rendered as *śīlavatī-anāthapiṇḍada*;
*anātha* is as explained above, and *piṇḍada* means "one who provides alms.
Volume eleven, translated in the Kingdom of Kucha, says: "to bend the body" (*kuṭilībhūta*).
The Mahāvaipulya Mahāsannipāta Sūtra, Volume 20: *Udyāna* (于填國) is translated as "Later Hall" (*yōnten*);
*Vida* (毘荼國) is translated as "Wisdom" (*chi*); *Abha* (遏波) is translated as "Small" (*shō*).
The Pañcavimśatisāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Volume 15: *Yabana* (耶般那) is translated as "Bondage" (*baku*).

The *Udrāyaṇarāja-sūtra* (translated by Jianfu) says “Good,” also called “Victorious. The *Tāmralipta* country (translated as “Delighting in the Dharma”). *Pārāli* country—this should be called *Pāṭalī*;
the translator says it is the name of a tree.
Volume eighteen: The *Cīnaśīla* country; *Cīna* means “diligence” and *Śīla* means “auspiciousness.”
The *Sūtra of the Wise and the Foolish*, Volume Two: Regarding "Visekandhi," it should be called "Visekandhi.
The translation states: "Visek" means "all-entrance" (*sarvāyatana*), and "Kandhi" means "sound.
Volume Three: Regarding "Bhadragiva," it should be called "Bhadrakīva."
The *Sūtra* says "Bhadrayus"; the translation says "Bhadrajīva. The country of Nyagrodha is translated as "Non-anger. Volume Nine:
the country of Rṣabha is translated as "Seer-Virtue" (*Ṛṣiśreṣṭha*). The country of Pāpālipura is translated as "Heavenly Power Full.
Volume Twelve: the land of Akṣobhya Buddha should be called Akṣobhya, or alternatively Akṣobhyavya.
Translated as: *The Sūtra of the Flower-Head of the Immovable*, Volume Ten; translated in the country of Amiluo. Translated as:
*The Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Precepts for Delighting in the Dharma*, Volume Two; translated in the country of Shaho. Translated as: *The Sūtra of Capable Endurance*.
The *Daśabhūmika-vibhaṅga-saṃyojana-sūtra*, Fascicle One, translated by Zhou Gou of the Kingdom of Chu;
"Luo" (落) is a transliteration of *vāsu*.
The *Vasumitra-sūtra*, Fascicle One; *Gautamī-nākulī* should be rendered as *Gautamī-nāḍī*.
The translation states: *Gautamī* is her clan name; *Nandā* is her personal name.
Regarding the fifth fascicle on lifespan, it was translated in the country of Avira, where it is rendered as "Lacking Diligence.
Regarding the fourth fascicle of the *Sūtra of One Hundred Parables*, it was translated in the country of Sikha, where it is rendered as "Victorious."
*The Sūtra of One Hundred Parables*, Volume Three: The Kingdom of Śrītīva;
translated as *Śrī* (Auspicious) and *Tīva* (Heaven). *Kalinga*: the translator states this is the name of a bird.
*The Upāsaka-śīla Sūtra*, Volume Five: The Kingdom of Rṣabha; it should be called *Rṣabhadeva*.
The translator says: *Sien-hsien pao-en ching*, Volume Two;
translated in the country of Mien-pi-li. The translator says: Is this emptiness or not?
*P'u-sa ch'ü-t'ai ching*, Volume Five; translated in the country of Mo-ch'a-ti. The translator says: A name for a star. That which is called Na-nan in the country [should actually be] Nanda.
Translated as: *The Sūtra on the Arising of Non-Joy*, Volume Two; translated in the country of Cīna (遮利國), meaning "movement.
Volume Five; *Kulūpa* (具留波) should be rendered as *Gulūpa* (瞿留波).
The translation states: *Gau* means "ox"; *Lūpa* means "color" (*varṇa*).

In the first fascicle of the *Guhyakapada-sūtra*, it is translated as "reliance" (*niśraya*) in the country of Spīlpa; in the third fascicle, it is translated as "seeking" (*mārga*) in the country of Śālupa;
and in the [third fascicle], it is translated as "resembling another" (*sadṛśa*) in the country of Śālupa.

The *Buddhacarita-kāvya*, Volume Two. Translated by Vidyākaraprabha. *Videha*: Videha means "the four regions. *Puri*: Puri means "city. *Ama-le-ka-pa*: Ama-le-ka means "stainless" (*vimala*). *Pa*: Pa means "resembling. *Śulopala*: Śulu means "hearing" (*śruta*). *Upala*: Upala means "protecting" (*pālana*). *Mahīpati*: Mahī means "earth. *Pati*:
Pati means "lord" (*adhipati*). *Parana*: Should be read as *Varaṇā*.

*Śi*: Śi is the name of a river. *Śitavika*: Should be read as *Śītadīghā*. *Śīta*: Śīta means "moon. *Dīghā*: Dīghā means "longest. *Bhaga*: Bhaga country means "seed" (*gotra*). *Mala*: Mala country means "flower" (*puṣpa*).

Fifth fascicle. *Suma* (須摩) is translated as "Moon" (*Candra*). *Āma* (阿摩) is translated as "Unripe. *Śūraṣeṇa* (首羅先那) is translated as "Hero. *Dhanapāla* (單夜槃耶) is translated as "Border. *Kāmpilya* (釰蒲闍) is translated as "Lovely. Regarding *Kapilavastu*, it should be called *Kapilavastu*. It is translated as follows:
*Kapila* means "azure-colored," and *vastu* means "dwelling place.
*Pūrvāparanidānasūtra* (過去現在因果經), one fascicle. *Thūlaccaya* (偷羅厥叉) should be called *Thūlaccaya*.

Translated as: *Mahāvaṃśa* (Great Lineage); *Lola* translated as "movement. *Sthūlakoṣṭha*: *Sthūla* means "large" and *koṣṭha* means "summit. *Bimbisāra*: *Bimba* means "image" and *sāra* means "victorious.
*Nālandā*: translated as the "Land of No-Leakage. *Uttarapāda*: *Uttara* means "not inferior," also called "superior";
*pāda* means "foot. *Tamāli*: translated as "Corydalis odorata. Volume Three: *Pāṅgu*: translated as "essential."
The *Nirvāṇa-sūtra in Two Parts*, Volume One; the *Candavimara-sūtra* states: "The brightness of the sun and moon.
The lower volume of the *Cūḍāmaṇi-sūtra*; the *Śikhaṇḍin-sūtra* states: "The pure appearance of the country of Śākya should be called Sāgara;
translated as 'Ocean'."
The *Nāgasena Sūtra*, Volume One, translated in the Kingdom of Sālā; "pool" (*tīrtha*).
The *Śāsana-samādhi Sūtra*, Volume Two, translated in the Buddha-field of Trimi; "tranquility" (*śānti*).
The *Tathāgata-tattva Sūtra*, Volume One, translated in the Kingdom of Vaimāda; "fear" (*bhaya*).
*The Adbhuta-dharma Sūtra*, Volume One. Translated by Mālava Ya (摩羅婆耶): *Māla* means "flower" (*puṣpa*), and *vaya* means "time" (*kāla*). Translated at the country of Vaiśālī:
*Vaiśālī* means "Unconquerable" (*aparājita*). Volume Two. Translated at the country of Mithilā—also called Mithila—meaning "Divided" (*vibhakta*).
The *Maitreya-buddha-sūtra* was translated at the kingdom of Kuntala; "Kuntala" is rendered as "Manya.
The *Dharmadundubhi-sūtra* was translated at the kingdom of Cālapa; "Cālapa" is rendered as "Xing" (Practice).
The *Kāśyapa-meets-the-Nirgrantha-sūtra* was translated at the kingdom of Rāmaka; "Rāmaka" is rendered as "Xixing" (Playful Practice).
The *Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha for King Prasenajit*, translated by Bāgùló; "Śakrabala" is translated as "Little Strength.

The *Sūtra of the Daughter of King Aśoka of the Kāntāha Realm*, translated as "Joyful Sound. The *Vimalkīya-kṣetra-sūtra* says it means "Free from Defilement and Turbidity. The kingdom of Kośambī is translated as "City.
The *Sūtra on the Bodhisattva Receiving the Upavāsa* [mentions] the realm of Pātālalañji, which should be called Pāṭhmapaṇalarañji.
The translation says: *Pāṭhama* is "lotus"; *vana* is "forest"; *rañjita* is "protected.
Regarding the *Dharmaguptaka-sūtra*, *khañjanā-nīla* should be rendered as *khañja-vana-nañjara*.
The translation says: *khañja* is "hidden"; *nañjara* is "not black. *Jaya* is the country name; the translation says it means "unconquerable."
The *Śrīmālā-sūtra*: "A-ho-ti" country should be called "Ābhāti," translated as "Not-to-be-discussed.
The *Anityatā-sūtra* of Kātyāyana: "Ga-zhou-la-jie" country should be called "Kapilavastu."
Translated as: *The Sūtra on King Cāṅcheng-liuli entering Hell*, translated in the great kingdom of Pārasī. Translated as:
*The Sūtra on the Pratyutpanna Samādhi*, translated in the kingdom of Mośudi. Translated as: *The Sūtra on Haoman*, translated in the kingdom of Dihuojie; it should properly be called Devanagara.
The translation [of the title] is *The Sūtra of King Aśoka of Devapura*; translated at Kuśinagara, it is called *Dì* (地).

The *Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Gaganagañja* was translated at Pāpā; it is called *Jìng* (淨). The *Sūtra of Rāma* was translated at Rāma; it is called *Xì* (戲). As for *Cakala*, it should be called *Cakara*.
The translation says: "Movement. The country of Vaiśālī should be called *Vaiśāli*;
the sūtra translates it as "to enter deeply. The country of Kapilavastu—the translator says it was the name of a seer—is the country of Piṇḍola; it should be called *Piṇḍola*. The translation says:
"*Piṇḍa*" means "truth" (*dṛḍha*) and "*Nala*" means "leakage" (*asrava*). The country of Rājagṛha is translated as: "*Rāja*" means "cause" (*hetu*) and "*Gṛha*" means "protection" (*rakṣa*)."
In the *Lokanirdeśa-sūtra*, the country of Yebha is translated as "Snake"; the country of Gandhāra should be called Gandhāratha, translated as "Fragrant Country.
In the *Saṃyukta-āgama*, the country of Gandhavatī should be called Gandhapāna.
Translated as "Fragrant Forest": the name of the country is Āraki.
Translated as "The Great General of the Hanging-Hair Deity’s Incantation Sūtra": the country is Gandhāra, which should be called *Gandharva*;
translated as "Smeller of Fragrance," also known as "Music Deity."
The *Sūtra on the Prince Dharmakāya* (Wangzi fayi jing) was translated at the country of Bārāvatī (Pōluoyue guó);
it should be called *Bārāvatī*, which is translated as "That Place.

The *Sūtra Asking the Four Boys about the Buddha* (Wen si tongzi jing) was translated at the country of Vidarbha (Bichu guó), which is translated as "Wisdom. The *Narakaṇḍa* (Nalogan-tuo guó) was translated as "Reed Cluster" (Dí zù).
*Satyasiddhi-śāstra*, Fascicle Nine: The *Kangqu* (康衢) translation states it is "Liyecun" (栗也村); the *Pocunposhi* (村婆村婆施) tradition states it is the "Foreign Country of Guojie" (國界外國).

*Fojingguo zhuan* (佛經國傳), Fascicle Two: The "Country of Many Countries" (*Guoduoguo*) translation states it is the "Country of Silence" (*Moyanguo*). *Kałasamok* (迦羅奢木) tradition: The "Country of Full Eagles and Gold" (*Manyingjinguo*). *Fascicle Four*:
The *Gashaguo* (伽沙國) translation states it is "Improper Speech" (*Buzhengyu*).

The First Volume of the *Lìguó zhuàn* (Records of Travels to Various Kingdoms): The Kingdom of Pāṭaliputra; translated as "Hù" (Guard). The Kingdom of Puṇṇavaddhana; translated as "Fēngmǎn" (Abundant and Full).

The Third Volume: The Kingdom of Kañci; translated as "Zàng" (Treasury). The Kingdom of Kāśī; translated as "Yǒuniú" (Possessing Cows). The Kingdom of Vārāṇasī; translated as "Zìzàixíng" (Autonomous Action). The Kingdom of Vatsa; translated as "Shéng" (Rope).
The Fourth Volume: The Kingdom of Anurādhapura; translated as "Huǒ" (Fire). Forty-fourth: Names of Cities. Vārāṇasī should be called Pōluónáhé; it is also written as Pōluónài.
The translator says: Jiangming.
The *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra*, Volume One: Vaiśālī is also called Vaiyālī;
translated as "Extensive Abode. The city of Śrāvastī should be called Śīlavatī; it is also called Śrāvastī.
The translator says: Regarding "Kāpilavastu," the abode of the ṛṣis, it should be called *Vilāsidu*, and is also called *Vilāvei*;
it is translated as "Kāpila" and "Vilāsidu" meaning "abode.
In the third fascicle, regarding "Gṛdhrakūṭa-parvata," it should be called *Gṛśinī*.
The translation says: "Mahāvinīta Pūrṇavardhana Mahānagara. It should be called *Pūrṇavardhana*.

The commentary says: "City of Long-Accumulated Merit. The translation says: "*Pūrṇa*" means "Full," and "*Bhadra*" means "Virtuous. "Ākīcchatrā Mahānagara" should be called *Ākīcchatrā*. The translation says:
"*Ākī*" means "Snake," and "*Cchatrā*" means "Umbrella. "Vakkalavatī Mahānagara" should be called *Vakkalavatī*, and is also called *Vakkala*.
The translation states: *Vakkalavati* means "existence. *Vakkhita* is also called *Vakkhida*;
the translation states it means "speech-banner. *Kosambī* is also called *Kosin*;

the translation states that *Kosa* means "treasury" and *Ambī* means "existence. *Kollagiri* is translated as "Kollagiri"; *Kolla* means "to act," or it refers to a clan name. *Pāṭaliputra* should be called *Pāṭaliputra*.

The translator says: *Pāṭali* is the name of a tree; *putra* means "son"; *Gandharva-nagara* is translated as "the city of the scent-eating gods" (*gandharva*), also called "the city of the music gods.
Volume six: *Brāhmaṇa-nagara* is translated as "the city of those who have transcended the mundane," also called "Pure Conduct.
Volume eight: *Śrāvastī* should be called *Śīlavatī*.
Translated as: *Śravaṇadhara* Yakṣa City. Translated as: *Puṣpadantī* (Flower-Eater) City.
*Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Fascicle Three. Translated as: *Garuḍa* City. Translated as: *Candrāvatāna* City. *Caṇdra* means "joy"; *avatāna* means "platform" or "altar. Fascicle Twenty-Four. Translated as:
*Kalingabaddhi* City. The translator states: *Kaliṅga* is the name of a bird; *baddhi* means "speech."
The forty-second fascicle: The city of Śobhāvatī is translated as "Śobhā" (Lovely) and "Vatī" (Guard). The city of Varavatī is translated as "Vara" (Superior) and "Vatī" (-ness).
Regarding the forty-third fascicle: The city of Varavatī should be called Vikaṭa;
it is translated as "Bare."
Volume Forty-nine. The City of Kuśinagara (also transcribed as Kuyīnà;
translated as "Small Reed").
*Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra*, Volume One. The City of Ujjayinī (translated as: *Uj* means "great" and *Jayanī* means "victorious").
Volume 14, Campā: The translator states that "campā" refers to the name of a flower.
Volume 27, Pūṇḍravardhana: The translator states that "pūṇḍra" means "foul odor.
Volume 29, Śivapura: The translator states that "śiva" means "peaceful security" and "pura" means "city."
In the thirty-first fascicle, "Kālapura" should be rendered as "Kālaśapura";
"Kālaśa" is translated as "Black" (Kāla) and "pura" as "city.
In the thirty-fifth fascicle, "Mithilā City" is translated as "Relaxation of the Mind."
The twenty-first fascicle of the *Ekottarika Āgama*, "Pāṭaligāma," should be rendered as "Pāṭaligrāma";
the translation is "Heavy-Store" (Chóngzhù).
The sixtieth fascicle of the *Madhyama Āgama*, "Vammīka," is translated as "Earth-Mound" (Dìyě).
The third fascicle of the *Dīrgha Āgama* was translated at the city of Kūṭi; "Kūṭi" means "weaving" and is also said to mean "tree.
The fourth fascicle was translated at the city of Vārāṇasī; "Vārāṇasī" means "leaping. The city of Aparāntaka should be called Aparas;
it is translated as "free from evil."
Volume Five: The city of Āpāṇḍava should be called *Āpaṃca*;
translated as "Without Aṅga. The city of Campā is translated as "Aṅga"; *aṅga* refers to the body, and *campā* refers to the tree. The city of Nandanā is translated as "Not Joyful.
Volume Twelve: Śūmabhadra is translated as "Moon-Long."
Volume Twenty: The city of Kāśī should be called Jiāshì;
the translation says "Light. The city of Mithilā is translated as "Golden Girdle.
The *Saṃyukta Āgama*, Volume Four: The city of Bandhumatī is translated as "Mùshì" (Muṣṭi).
Volume Eleven: Saṃkāśya City; translated as "Light.
Volume Seventeen: Pāpī City; it should be written as Pāpī, translated as "Evil."

The Preface to the *Daśabhāṇavāra-vinaya*, Volume One. Translated at the city of Bhadrapattī; "Bhadrapattī" is translated as "City of Worthy Speech. At the city of Aṭaṅka; "Aṭaṅka" is translated as "City of Ghosts and Spirits.
The Fourth Volume on the Seven Dharmas. Translated at the city of Bhadrapattī;
"Bhadrapattī" is translated as "Discourse. The Sixth Volume. Translated at the city of Śrāvastī; it should be called Śrāvastī (Śrāvastī).
The translation says: "The Fruit of the Fine Tree.
At the beginning of the eighth fascicle, "Śobhavatī" city should be rendered as "Śobha.
The translation says: "Śobha" means "lovely."
*Ekottarika-āgama*, Volume 1, translated at the city of Devavatī: *deva* means "heaven" (*deva*), and *vatī* means "virtuous" (*bhadra*).
*Dharmaguptaka-vinaya*, Second Part, Volume 9, translated at the city gate of Śikhā: *śikhā* means "victory" (*jaya*), or alternatively, "topknot" (*keśa*).
Volume 10, translated at the city of Pāṭaliputra: [The term] *apabhāṣita* means "incorrect speech. Regarding *Vāruṇasabha*, it should be rendered as *Lokākṣa*.
Translated as: *Zhòngguī* (The Weighted Turtle), Fourth Division, Volume Six; *Bátíluóchéng* (City of Bāṭikā) should be translated as "Worthy" (*báti*).
The fourth fascicle of the Mahīśāsaka-vinaya, translated at Takṣaśilā City;
the eighth fascicle concerning Paṭaliputra City— this should be called Vardhamāna,
translated as "Encircling."
The *Abhidharma-vibhāṣā-śāstra*, Volume 23, translated at the city of Pāpī; "Pāpī" means "evil.
Volume 46, translated at the city of Nadika; "Nadi" means "river" and "Kaya" means "country.
Volume 54, translated at the city of Śrīgupta; "Śrīgupta" means "unconditioned" (*asaṃskṛta*).
*Vibhāṣā*, Volume Nine. Translated at the city of Bharukaccha. "Bharu" means sand; "kaccha" means hair.
*The Sutra of the Wise and the Foolish*, Volume Eight. The city of Dhūtakara should be called Dhūtakāra;
it is translated as "Ascetic Practice."
The Sutra of One Hundred Parables, Volume Four: The Great City of Kuśinagara should be called *Kuśinagarī*;
translated as "Grass City. The City of Bandhumatī Śrāvastī; translated as "Bandhu" meaning "place of kinship" and "Śrāvastī" meaning "the dwelling place of Bodhisattvas.
The City of Aṅga-Puṇḍravardhana from the *Bodhisattva Garbha Sūtra*, Volume One; translated as "Body City."
The *Buddhacarita*, Fascicle Four. *Pāpā*: translated as "Pure. *Kuśāgrapura*: translated as "City of the Tip of Grass.
*Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra*, Fascicle One. *Bhāndhumatī*: should be called *Bhāndumatī*;
translated as "Having Kin."
The *Xingqixing jing* (Sūtra on the Arising of Practice), translated by Bāṣpottara, states that "zhù" (聚) means "assembly.
The *Ānòufēng jīng* (Sūtra on the Ānòu Wind) states that "zhāntuómótí" (栴頭摩提) should be rendered as "zhāntuómǔdì" (栴他摩底),
which is translated as "evil intention."
The *Buddhabhāṣita-prabhāsa-sūtra* (佛說光華經), translated at Kapilavastu (迦毘羅城);
"Cang" (蒼) is the translation for [the city's name]. The *Ākāśagarbha-bodhisattva-sūtra* (觀虛空藏菩薩經), translated by Dharmarakṣa (達摩那伽羅).
The *Sīvana-sūtra* (縫衣經), [translated at] Ketumatī (翅頭末城)—it should properly be called Ketumati (翅兜摩底).
The translation is titled *The Sūtra on Maitreya Becoming a Buddha at the City of Pukara*. It is also called *The Lotus Miscellany Sūtra*.
Regarding "Sūratapippalā": "Sūrata" means a good country, and "Pippalā" refers to a yellowish-red color. According to the *Tradition of the Garden of Compassion*, it is called "Stone City."

The First Fascicle of the *Foreign Records* (*Waiguo Zhuan*): The Biography of Śrāvastī states: "New City. The Biography of Pāṭaliputra states: "A salty land. The Biography of Kārvaṭa states: "Entering the City of Clouds. The Biography of Vaiśālī states: "The City of the Full Great Man. The Biography of Āḷavī states: "The Hunting City. The Second Fascicle:

The Biography of Vairambhya states: "The City of the Great Drum. The Biography of Tāmraliptī states: "The City of the Hollow Hole. The Biography of Sāketa states: "The New Wood City. The Biography of Puṇḍravardhana states: "The Gathered Land. The Biography of Bhadranagara states: "The Famous City. The Biography of Āgaru states: "The City of Single-Rice-Straw. The Biography of Rājagṛha states: "The Red Cloud City. The Biography of Cālukya states: "Fine White Cotton. The Biography of Aṅga states: "The City of the Viper Snake. The Biography of Mathurā states: "The City Without Wine."

The third fascicle, the *Biography of Kaṇauj*, states: "The City of High Shoulders. The *Biography of Tilā* states: "The City of Broken Peaks. The *Biography of Ārāvi* states: "The City of the Vast Marsh. The *Biography of Kumārapura* states: "The City of the Camp. The *Biography of Sūhañja* states: "The City of Long-enduring Patience. The *Biography of Aludā* states: "The City Without Weeping. The *Biography of Guṇākara* states: "The City of Constant Existence. The *Biography of Baddhamāna* states: "The City of Abundant Benefit. The *Biography of Anupatana* states: "The City of Abundant Fulfillment. The *Biography of Mālī* states: "The City of Perfumed Ointments. The *Biography of Yakkhalaṅkā* states: "The City of Monetary Value. The *Biography of Aparanta* states: "The City of Encamped Walls."

In the fourth fascicle, the city of Pāṭalī is translated as "Lotus City. The city of Bāluka is translated as "Layered. The city of Kharjūra is translated as "Splitting City. The city of Vakra is translated as "Curved. The city of Kurapaṭa is translated as "Hawk City. The city of Bhadravati is translated as "Supreme City. The city of Mahādoṭṭaka is translated as "Great Mouth City. The city of Tamranaga is translated as "Copper City. The city of Varuṣa is translated as "Victorious Abode.
In the first fascicle of the *Lìguó zhuàn* (Record of Travels through Countries), the city of Nāgāhva is translated as "Dragon-Love.

The city of Pauruṇa is translated as "Viper. In the third fascicle, the city of Vetrasa is translated as "Four Reeds. The city of Mahāśa is translated as "Great Joy" (five tones). The city of Dravida is translated as "Tree Name. The city of Vaṅga should be called "Bengga."
The translation says: *Śākya* is also called *Kubajha*; *Nagarahāra* should be translated as *Bajhanagara*. *Bajha* means "long," and *nagara* means "city.
*Sumaṇabhūmi* is translated as "City of the Golden Pitcher" (*Suvarṇakumbhī*). *Mathurā* is translated as "Beautiful. *Saṃkāśya* is translated as "Radiance.
*Tāmalipti* should be called *Tāmralipti*, translated as "Attached to Pleasure. Chapter Forty-five: Names of Towns. *Tāmbuliputra* should be called *Yatāliputrā*.
Translated as: *Eḍakarika* (Eḍaka-ṛṣi); *Putrapradāna* (Son-giving). *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Volume 24;
translated at the city of Aṇuvāji; translated as: "Without Many Companions.
*Madhyama Āgama*, Volume 27; translated at the city of Bhadravati; translated as: "Worthy Speech" (*Bhadra-vādin*).
The *Daśabhāṇavāra-vinaya*, third recitation, fourth fascicle, translated by Kajili Dayi: "Kajuri" means "Mountain Monastery.
The *Mahāsāṃghika-vinaya*, thirtieth fascicle, translated by Kalanda Yiyi: "Kālāndaka" means "Fine Sound.
The *Mahīśāsaka-vinaya*, first fascicle, translated by Vajji Yiyi: "Vajji" means "Gathering. The *Aṭavi* district: "Aṭavi" means "Forest."
The third fascicle: *Pāveyya* is translated as "Possessing Wisdom.
The fifth fascicle: *Vajjī* should be rendered as *Sakyeya*, translated as "Welcome.
*Ujeṇī* is translated as "Worthy of Victory. *Bhaddiya* should be rendered as *Bhadrapāṇa*.
Translated as "The Grove of the Wise," Volume Twelve;
translated at the town of Anāpinī as "The Dropless," Volume Twenty-Six;
translated at the town of Kūli as "Weaving."
The Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra, Volume One of the Two-Volume Edition, translated by Bhadrapāla at the city of Bādara.
The Sūtra on the Characteristics of the Five Precepts for Upāsakas, No. 46. The Village Name, No. 46. Nāla Village; “Nāla” is translated as Reed.
The Mahāprajñāpāramitā Śāstra, Volume One. Uruvilvā Village; “Uruvilvā” is translated as Wood-apple.
The third fascicle: *Sāla-grāma*. The translator states that "Sāla" is the name of a tree.
The twenty-seventh fascicle: *Bala-grāma*. The translator states that "Bala" means "victorious.
The eighty-fourth fascicle: *Pāda-grāma*. The translator states that "Pāda" means "foot."
*Saṃyukta Āgama*, Volume 2, translated at the village of Droṇa; the translator notes that "Droṇa" is the name of a tree and is also used as a surname.
Volume 14, [translated at] the village of Varana; it should be read as *Varana*, translated as "Barley."
Volume 14: *Sātū-grāma*, translated as "Good.
Volume 21: *Nalika-grāma*, translated as "Excessively Carved.
Volume 40: *Balinā-grāma*; it should be called *Pāriyātra*.
Translated as "The Time of Play," Volume 43;
translated as "Various Offerings," Village of Vairambhya, Volume 37;
translated as "Past Time," Village of Uruvilvā.
In the forty-fourth fascicle, the village name *Na-laṅkāra* should be rendered as *Na-laṅgā-li*;
the translator notes that this is the name of a flower.
In the forty-seventh fascicle, the village name *Maṇicūḍa* is translated as "Jewel Topknot" (*Bǎo fà*); it is also like a "jewel topknot" (*zhū fà*).
The Preface to the *Daśabhāṇavāra-vinaya*, Volume One. Translated at the village of Piṇḍaśāla; "Piṇḍaśāla" means "Frequenting the Sand.
The *Mahāsāṃghika-vinaya*, Volume Twenty-nine. Translated at the village of Puṣkaravatī; "Puṣkaravatī" means "Lotus. Volume Thirty.
Translated at the village of Bhadraśālā; "Bhadraśālā" means "King of Heaven."
The ninth fascicle of the third division of the *Dharmaguptaka-vinaya* (the *Uruvilvā-grāma* section) should be called *Uruvilvā*;
translated as "Great Hero.
The nineteenth fascicle of the *Mahīśāsaka-vinaya* (the *Uruvilvā-sena-grāma* section) should be called *Uruvilvā-sena*.
The translation says: Mahāvīra (Great Hero). Rājagṛha (City of the King) is the name of a brahmin village;
it should be called *Duti*, which translates as "to decide. Ālakā village translates as "Hanging Hair," and is also said to mean "Victorious.
*Samantapāsādikā* (Vinaya-vibhāṣā), Volume Twelve. Susumāragira translates as "Level Body."
The fourth fascicle of the *Lalitavistara Sūtra*, translated at the village of Vairaṇyā; "Vairaṇyā" is translated as "Tranquility.
The lower fascicle of the *Mahāyānopāya-kauśalya Sūtra*, translated by Bhaṅgaja; "Bhaṅgaja" refers to the name of a country.
The *Śīlasamprayukta Sūtra*, translated at the village of Droṇa; it should rather be called "Pakvoḷa."
The translator says: This is the name of a tree.
In the *Sūtra on the Appearance of the Two Banner-Wheels at the Buddha’s Footprint*, it is the village of Tāla; the translator says this is the name of a tree.
In the *Mañjuśrī-nirvāṇa Sūtra*, it is the village of Carakara-cūḍaka-naraka; "Caraka" means moving, "Cūḍaka" means small, and "Naraka" means person.
In the *Bāharī-dvīpa-buddha-prasannadeva-pūrvayoga-sūtra*, "Bāharī" is translated as "Pāṭalī"; the translator notes that this is the name of a tree.

In the forty-seventh [chapter] of the *Brahmajāla-sūtra*, "Naraka-grāma" (the village of Naraka) is translated as "Nāra. It is the name of a village; it is the forty-seventh [chapter]. "Nāra" is translated as "Nāra."
The *Ekottarika Āgama*, fascicle 11: *Videha* should be pronounced *Videha*;
translated as "affliction," it is also called "various bodies.
The *Madhyama Āgama*, fascicle 10: *Yantu* is translated as "purple. *Vibhaṅgi* should be pronounced *Vibhaṅgi*.
Translated as: "Not fond of form" (12th fascicle). *Sālarūla* should be called *Sālarūla*;
translated as: *Sāla* means "real," and *Rūla* means "moving."
Volume Seventeen, translated by Shuluta: "Shu" means "to hear.
Volume Forty-one, "Ajara-ho-ni," should be called "Ajara-va-na," which translates as "Forest Without Nets.
"Śamī" translates as "tranquility."
Fascicle 52: *Sena* (斯那) is translated as "army" (*senā*) or "valiant" (*śūra*).
Fascicle 56: *Nada* (那陀) is translated as "sound. *Dīrgha Āgama*, Fascicle 2:
*Āmra* (菴婆羅) is said by the translator to be the name of a fruit; *Campaka* (瞻婆) is said by the translator to be the name of a flower.

The third fascicle: *Gandha* is translated as "fragrance"; *Bhūmi* is translated as "earth"; *Pippala-grāma* is translated by the commentator as the name of a tree; *Ukkala-grāma* is translated as "majestic power.
Fascicle thirteen: *Khāṇu-vatī* should be read as *Khātu-vatīśa*;
the commentator states that *khāṇu* means "stump" and *vatīśa* means "to speak."
Fifteenth fascicle: *Bāra Village*, translated as "Victorious.
Seventeenth fascicle: *Rāma Village*, translated as "Play," also called "King.
*Saṃyukta Āgama*, Fascicle Twenty-three: *Uppala General Village*, translated as "Great Cave," also called "Great Hero."
In the ninth fascicle of the second division of the *Dharmaguptaka-vinaya*, "Bhaṅgī Village" should be read as "Mṛgaśīrṣa";
the translation is "The Crooked.
In the eighth fascicle of the fourth division, "Caṇḍāla Village" is translated as "The Moon."
The *Sūtra-vibhāṣā-śāstra* (Shanjian lü pípóshā), Volume One: The village of Vidiśā should be called Vidiśā;
translated as "the four contemplations.
Volume Two: The Brahmin village of Bakula; Bakula is the name of a tree.
Volume Three: Lohinā Village; translated as "Long" (pronounced *zhāng yǔ fǎn*). Kalandaka Village; the Vinaya states it means "mountain mouse. The Translator says: [This is] the name of a bird.
Volume Six: Ugga Village; translated as "Without Public Regulation.
Volume Sixteen: Uruvilvā Village; translated as "Wood Melon."
The *Abhidharma-vibhāṣā*, Volume One; translated at the village of Pāpā (translated as "Great Power").
The eighteenth volume of the *Mahāvaipulya-mahāsannipāta-sūtra*; [mentions] the village of Kuśinagara (should be called Kuśināgara), translated as "Grass City."
*Chuyao jing* (Udānavarga), Volume 10, translated by Youloutina: *Youla* means "chest" (*ura*), and *Tidina* means "bestowal.
*Za ahan* (Saṃyuktāgama), Volume 21: *Ajieloustou* should be called *Angarastūpa*.
The *Jing* says: "Charcoal Stūpa."
Volume Forty-two, translated at the Vibhāra Vihāra, titled *The Vinaya of the Mahāsāṃghikas* (Shèngù Sēngqī Lǜ), Volume One;
translated at the Kūliyana Vihāra, titled *The Vinaya of the Mahāsāṃghikas* (Zhìyě Sēngqī Lǜ), Volume One;
translated at the Pesi Grotto, titled *The Vinaya of the Mahāsāṃghikas* (Chuǎilái); and translated at the Mathurā Grove Vihāra, titled *The Vinaya of the Mahāsāṃghikas* (Mìyě).
The eighth fascicle, *Zhāotí Sēngtáng* (Monastery of the Monks from the Four Quarters):
"Zhāotí" means the four quarters. The twelfth fascicle of the *Mahīśāsaka-vinaya*, *Chébōluótǎ*: "Chébōluó" means movement.
The twenty-fourth fascicle, *Bīdixià Sì*: it should be written as *Pídìjié*.
The translator says:
"The *Sudarsana-vinaya-vibhāṣā*, Volume Two, translated at the Maheśvara Monastery; 'Maheśvara' means 'Great Sovereign.
Volume Three, translated at the Pūrva Saṃghārāma; it should be called 'Pūrṇa.'"
The translation states: *Purva* refers to the Eastern Monastery, as explained above in the fifth fascicle;
*Purvarāma* should be translated as "Eastern Garden.
*Gautama-chaitya* is translated as "Temple of the Gautama Clan"; it is translated as "Garden" because it is the clan name.
In the fourteenth fascicle, *tūpa* should be rendered as *sītūpa*;
the translation is "stūpa.
In the ninth fascicle of the *Vibhāṣā*, *yakṣa-āyatana* is translated as "capable" (*nenggǎn*).
*Chuyao jing* (Sūtra of the Exalted Utterances), Volume 5, translated at Pāṇa Monastery; "zhong" (seed).
Volume 10, translated at Saṃghama Monastery; "qiaoqiupo" (Kapphina).
*Xumijing* (Sūtra of Sumati), Volume 5, translated at Chabala Monastery; it should be called "Shuge'la."
The *Sūtra* says "turning" (*zhuǎn*); the *Yì* says "turning" (*zhuǎn*).

The *Kṣudrakavastu* (*Qián dù*) compiled by Bodhisattva Vasumitra, translated at Ātāpī Monastery—Ātāpī means "forest"—Volume Six of the *Mātṛkā*, concerning the Nyagrodha Vihāra; it should be called Nyagrodha.
Translated as:
*The Sūtra on the Samādhi of Contemplating the Buddha in All Directions*, Volume One. Translated at Karuṇā Monastery;
"Karuṇā" should be rendered as "Karavāna," meaning "Village Forest."
The *Nāgasena Sūtra*, Volume One, translated at the Tāpasa-guṭhā Vihāra. "Tāpasa" means an elder ascetic; "guṭhā" means a bird-venom spell.
The *Gaṅgika Sūtra* was translated at the Gaṅgika Vihāra; the translator states that this is the name of a country.
The *Saṃyukta Sūtra* and the *Nāma-vihāra Biography* state that "Saṃyukta" refers to a monastery.
*Wai Guo Zhuan*, Fascicle 1; translated at Nalada Village (translated as *Di*).
*Sengqielachasuo Ji Jing*, Fascicle 3; translated at Tanamati Village (translated as *Tanazhe* for *Dāna* and *Madi* for *mati*;
"The Buddha’s Deeds"). *Fosoxingzan*, Fascicle 4; translated at Viśeṣa Village (should be rendered as *Viseju Sheta*).

The translator says: *Vijaya* is the name of a country; *Ṣṭha* means "victory"; *Bhadrika-grāma* is translated as "Long" (the rhyme is *zhāngyǔ*); *Vairañjaka-grāma* is translated as "Non-attachment"; *Kālimasa-grāma* is translated as "Evil," or also called "Black";
*Vijaya-grāma* should be called *Vaiśeṣika*, translated as "All-entrances.
In the fifth fascicle, *Pāpali-grāma* is translated as "Spot."
The Sutra on Cause and Effect of Past and Present, Volume Three, translated by Daboli Cun as *Hu* (Guardian).
The Lower Volume of the Dharma Drum Sutra, translated by Aza Sha, which should be called Amu Sha,
as *Budong* (Immovable).
"Water-foam Drifting" (Suǐmò suǒpiāo) is translated as *Lāmaka* Village; it means "Play.
The *Sūtra on the Buddha’s Supernatural Power Saving the Son of a Householder* (Fóshénlì jiù zhǎngzhězǐ jīng) states that *Vatamaṇa* is transmitted as "Increasing" (*Zēngyì*) Village.

In the second volume of the *Foreign Traditions* (Wàiguó zhuàn), *Dāpídá* is transmitted as "Forest Without Supernatural Powers" (*Wútōng lín*). The *Tradition of the Hālī Monastery* (Hélí gānlán zhuàn) calls it "Holy Forest" (*Shèng lín*). The *Tradition of the Vihelgaḷa* (Bǐhuìgālán zhuàn) calls it "Grain-Seed" (*Gǔzhǒng*) Village. The *Tradition of Rājavihāra* (Luóshā pīhéhé zhuàn) calls it "Monastery Village. 48. Names of Monasteries, Part Fourteen: The Jetavana Vihāra should be called *Jetavanana*.
The translation states: *Śītavana* means "Cold Forest.

The *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra*, Volume Three, translated at the Viśvantara Vihāra. The translation states: *Viśvantara* means "Sage" (*ṛṣi*), and *Vana* means "Garden" (*ārāma*). The translator states: it is the name of a country. The *Suvarṇapradīpa Saṃghārāma*. The translation states:
*Saṃghārāma* means "Grove of the Assembly. The twenty-fourth volume of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*: *Cakravāḍa*; it should be called *Cakrapāla*.
The translation says: "Movement.
The *Madhyama Āgama*, Volume 35, translated by Kālayaśas; "Kāla" means time.
The [same] volume 49, translated by Gñan-dru; "Gñan-dru" means a gathering of the assembly.

The fiftieth fascicle, the *Biography of Rājavihāra*, states it is the King’s Monastery (*Rājavihāra*). The *Biography of Devavihāra* states it is the Prince’s Monastery (*Devavihāra*). The *Biography of Maṇama* states it is the Gao-fan Monastery (*Gao-fan-vihāra*). The *Biography of King Kaniska* states it is the King’s Secondary Monastery (*Rājadvitīyavihāra*). The *Biography of Navavihāra* states it is the Mixed Monastery (*Miśravihāra*). Fascicle Four:

The *Biography of Vīra* states it is the Divine Grain Monastery (*Devadhānyavihāra*). The *Biography of Devabhūti* states it is the Prince’s Vihāra (*Devabhūtivihāra*). Regarding the monastery of Śāvika, etc., the translation says "Abandoning Poison" (*Poison-Dispelling*). In the first fascicle of the *Record of Travels through Various Kingdoms*:
The *Bala Monastery* is translated as "Protection" (*Gupta*). The *Leyue Monastery* should be called *Revata*.
The translation says: "Star Name" (Xingming) refers to the monastery named Dhavalinda;
it should be called Dhavalindama. The tradition says: "Shiliu Yijia Yan" (石留一迦延) refers to the monastery named Ekamārga. "Apohiri" (阿婆耆梨) refers to the monastery named Abhayagiri;
the tradition says it is the "Fearless Monastery. Volume Four: "Mahabihuo" (摩呵比呵) refers to the monastery named Mahāvihāra.
The translation says: *Mahāvihāra* (Great Monastery); it should be called *Jinabihāra*, which is translated as "Victorious Forest Monastery.

This is the forty-ninth [section], titled "Names of Halls and Quarters. Regarding the *Viśākha Hall*, the translator says: "Viśākha" is the name of a lunar mansion (*nakṣatra*) from which great wisdom was born.
In the forty-third fascicle of the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra*, regarding the *Vimāna room*, the translation says: "Palace."
In the first fascicle of the fourth division of the *Dharmaguptaka-vinaya*, "Āmra-cīvara" should be rendered as "Āmrapālī";
it is translated as "tree-heart.
In the first fascicle of the *Sudarśana-vinaya-vibhāṣā*, "Kanakavana" is translated as "gold."
Volume Three: *Khandakūṭa*, translated as "Fragrant Chamber," "Fragrant Terrace," or "Fragrant Palace"; *Skandhāravatī*, translated as "Palace of the Mother of Shoulders" or "The Commoner.
Volume Five: *Kālī*, translated as "The Maker" or "The Black One.
*Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra*, Volume One: *Cakravartin*, translated as "Wheel-Turner."
*Ajātaśatru-sūtra*, lower fascicle; "Kāla-vrata" (迦羅越) in the household should be rendered as "Kāla-bha" (迦羅婆), translated as "at times.
*Yi-jiao san-mei jing* (遺教三昧經), upper fascicle; "Kālīra" (迦梨羅) hall is translated as "turbid" (濁).
The *Mañjuśrī-bhāṣita-ratnakaraṇḍa-sūtra*, Volume I, translated by Xuli (須梨) at the Jingtang (講堂):
"Ji" (日) means "sun. The *Arthavargīya-sūtra*, Volume II, translated by Kali (迦梨) at the Jingtang: "Shi" (時) also means "time," or "to act.
The *Nandika-sūtra* commentary by Alukshara (阿陸舍羅) states: "She" (舍) means "freedom from illness. 50. The Name of the Location, Number Fifty: *Āraṇya*, also called *Aranya*.
Translated as:
*The Treatise on Tranquil Great Wisdom*, Fascicle Three. Regarding the term *Tilabhakṣa*:
it should be translated as *Śrāvakas*. "Śrā" means "to hear," and "vaka" means "room."

The twenty-fourth fascicle of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, translated by Zhiyan and Quchu: "Zhiye" (治耶) means "Swift Movement" (*kṣipragāmin*); "Nadī" (那提) means "Sound"; "Ghaṇṭā" (楗椎) means "Bell. The tenth fascicle of the *Dīrgha Āgama*:
"Kalmāṣa" (劫摩沙) should be called "Kalmāṣa" (釰摩沙); it is translated as "Removal of Leaves.
"Indrapura" (因陀波羅) is translated as "Principal Power. "Urvilvā" (欝鞞羅) is translated as "Past Time. "Ayodhyānī" (阿遊婆陀尼) should be called "Aśmaparāntī" (阿細波陀尼).
Translated as "No Seeking," Āṭānāṭiya; translated as "Following Practice," Volume Ten;
Icchānaṅgala, translated as "Delighting in Plowing," Volume Twelve;
Kūṭāgāra, translated as "Weaving."
Volume 18. Translated by Jīvaka Kumārabhṛta. *Jīva* means life, also translated as longevity (*āyus*). *Kumāra* means youth. The *Saṃyukta Āgama*, Volume □, translated by Kāḷaka:
*Kaliṅga* means "beautiful voice," also translated as the name of a country. Volume 9, translated by Puṇyatrāta:
*Bhaṅgaja* means "turning back," also translated as the name of a country. *Devīda* is translated as "ignorance."
Volume Ten, translated by Shuluna; "Shu" means "to hear.
Volume Twelve, Pāṭaliputra; it should be called Pāṭaliputtra.
The translator states: "Pāṭali" is the name of a tree, and "puttra" means "son."
Volume 21: *Nata-badzhika* is translated as "Dance" (*nata*) and "Army" (*badzhika*).
Volume 24: *Vilanya* is translated as "Not Tranquil.
*Dharmāraṇya* (from the *Dharmaguptaka-vinaya*, Volume 1) is translated as "Dharma-Quiescence" (*dharmāraṇya*).
*Abhidharma-vibhāṣā*, Fascicle 27: *Vajrapuṣpa*; translated as "Vajra-ground.
*Bāśumati-sūtra*, Fascicle 5: *Pārāṇa*; translated as "Name of a country."
The Buddhacarita-kāvya, Fascicle Four. Translated by Jñānagupta at Némoluo: titled the *Vimala-utpatti-carita-sūtra*, Upper Fascicle.
Translated by Varṇamitra: titled the *Viśeṣa-lakṣaṇa-nātha-vajrika-āraṇya*. Regarding "Nātha," it means "Dancer"; "Vajrika" means "General"; "Āraṇya" means "Silent Place.
The *Śreṣṭhi-putra-sūtra* translated by Kumārajīva: titled "Thus It Was Said."

The Mahāśūramgama-samādhi Sūtra, translated from the Sanskrit, Volume Eight. Completed copying on the fifth day of the third month in the second year of the Nintei era. On the twenty-sixth day of the eighth month in the first year of the Kōho era, the cyclical year being *Kinsyu* (辛酉), this was collated and finalized using the manuscript of the Master Shin-gen.
Recorded by the Chief Monk (Sōjō) Gen-ka, fifty-eighth [in the series].
Translated from the Sanskrit, Volume Nine.
Fifty-one: Mountain Names; Fifty-two: River Names;

Fifty-three: Stream Names; Fifty-four: Lake Names; Fifty-five: Island Names; Fifty-six: Land Names; Fifty-seven: Water Names; Fifty-eight: Fire Names; Fifty-nine: Wind Names; Sixty: Garden Names; Sixty-one: Forest Names; Sixty-two: Tree Names. 51. Mountain Names: Mount Sumeru (Sumeru) should be called Sumeru-lou.
The translation says: *Sumeru* means "excellent name.
Regarding *Mahāmeru*, the first fascicle of the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra* translates it as "Mount Moli. *Gṛdhrakūṭa* should be translated as *Gṛdhrakūṭa*;
*gṛdhra* means "vulture" and *kūṭa* means "peak," thus it is translated as "Vulture Peak. *Gṛdhrakūṭa* means "the peak of the vultures."
The third fascicle: *Vipra* should be rendered as *Vipara*, translated as "Little Strength" (*Śaukra*).
*Bāhuśruta* should be rendered as *Bāhuja*, translated as "Calf," or alternatively called a "clan name. *Satyabuddhi* should be rendered as *Satyaprajña*.

The translation says: *Saptaparṇa* means "seven-leaved. *Guhā* means "cave. *Indra* means "Heavenly King. *Śaila-guhā* means "mountain-cave"; *śaila* means "mountain" and *guhā* means "cave. *Sādhya* means "to be accomplished. *Parvata* means "peak" or "section.
*Yugandhara*—also called *Yugandhī*—means "Yugandhara"; *yu* means "pair" and *gandhara* means "to hold. *Kaśmīra-vardhana* should be rendered as *Kaśmīra-vardhana*;
*kaśmīra* means "Kashmir" and *vardhana* means "increase. *Mahā-meru* means "Great Mountain. *Mahā* means "great."
The twenty-eighth fascicle: *Cakravāḍa* (Mount) is translated as "Wheel.
The first fascicle of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*: *Khadiraka* (Mountain) should be read as *Khadira*;
it is translated as "Kha" meaning "to dig into the earth" and "Dira" meaning "to break."
Volume Twenty-two: Mount Nimindhara; "Nimiṃdha" is translated as "Earth," and "dhara" is translated as "Holder. Mount Mucilinda, also called Mukhaliṃda, is translated as "Liberation.
Volume Twenty-four: Mount Udayagiri; it is translated as "The Place Where the Sun First Rises. Mount Mahāmucilinda is translated as "Great Liberation."
The twenty-eighth fascicle, Mount Vipula, is translated as "Great.
The eighteenth fascicle of the *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra*, Mount Udayana, is translated as "Place of Sunrise.
The twenty-fourth fascicle, Mount Malaya, is also called Malayana.
The translation states: *Māra* means "defilement"; *Jaya* means "removal.
Volume twenty-nine: Mount Mandara; the translation states it is also called "Protection," or Mount Aṭavī.
Volume thirty: Mount Śiśumāra; the translation states it means "killing the child."
In the third fascicle of the *Ekottarika Āgama*, Mount Pāṣa is also called Pāṣana,
translated as "rope.
In the thirteenth fascicle, Mount Maśī is translated as "black."
Volume Fourteen: Mount Īśa, translated as *Īśvara* (Sovereign). Volume Twenty-three:

Mount Vinaya, translated as *Tathāgata* (Thus-Come One). Mount Ujjayanta, translated as *Buddha* (Awakened). Mount Bandhuma, translated as *Sūrya* (Sun), or alternatively the clan name *Bhāradvāja*, which should be rendered as *Bharadvāja*;
translated as "May one obtain [fulfillment]."
In the eighth fascicle of the *Madhyama Āgama*, "Vidha" is translated as "wisdom.
In the tenth fascicle of the *Dīrgha Āgama*, "Gagara" is translated as "glue.
In the eighteenth fascicle, "Iṣadhāra" is translated as "sovereign-holder," and "Uccantagiri" is translated as "greatly victorious. "Śiṃśapāvana" is translated as "without greatness."
Volume Twenty-one: Piśitācala, translated as "Transformation"; Utpalavarnā, translated as "Great Upholder.
Volume Twenty-two: Śiśupālā, which should be Śiśupālā, translated as "Child Protector."
In the fifth fascicle of the *Saṃyukta Āgama*, *Makula* is translated as "noisy"; *Vinataka* is translated as "Gandha";
and in the sixteenth fascicle, *Urumaṇḍa* is translated as "Uru" or "Great Maṇḍa," while *Citra* is also called "Real.

In the twenty-third fascicle, *Kanthamādhava* is translated as "Fragrant Flower"; *Vakra* is translated as "Crooked" or also as the name of a country; *Śūpa* is translated as "Axe"; *Vipula* is translated as "Powerless"; and *Nāga-parvata* is translated as "Pillar."
Volume Forty-five: *Ti-ti-he* (Ṭiṭibha), translated as "Various Bodies," also called the "Fourth Meditation.
Volume Fifty: *Mo-ju-lo-shan* (Makula-parvata), translated as "Heavenly Crown.
*Daśabhāṇavāra-vinaya*, Recitation Three, Volume Three: *Pin-jia-shan* (Piñjā-parvata); it should be called *Pin-ta* (Piṇḍa).

Translated as: *The Sixth Fascicle on the Seven Methods of Archery and Libation*, translated by Sappavara-parvata. "Sappa" means "all"; "vara" means "suffering"; "kṣudra" means "small. Translated as: *Saptana-guhā-parvata*. "Saptana" means "enemy"; "guhā" means "cave. It should be [correctly] called *Sarva-saṃskāra-parvata*.

That [previous] translation was: "Sarva" means "all"; "saṃskāra" means "to refine or treat"; "parvata" means "mountain. Translated as: *Sapta-patra-guhā-parvata*. "Sapta" means "seven"; "patra" means "leaf"; "guhā" means "cave. Translated as: *Kāśi-kṛṣṇa-parvata*. "Kāśi" means "light."
The *Mahāsāṃghika-vinaya*, Volume Seven, translated at Mount Cetiya; "Cetiya" is rendered as "Gathering" (or "State").
Volume Thirty: translated at Mount Māla; "Māla" is rendered as "Succession of Practice" (or "Flower Garland").
Volume Thirty-Two: *Kīra-su*; it should be read as *Kīra-pa*.
The translation says:
"White," the thirty-fourth fascicle; Mount Haridraka—the translation says: "Yellow.
The *Dharmaguptaka-vinaya*, Second Part, Ninth Fascicle; Mount Mathurā—the translation says: "Mathu" means "secret" (*guhya*) and "rā" means "clan" (*gotra*).
Volume Eleven, translated at Mount Kukkutapāda (*Kukkuṭapabbata*). "Kukkuṭa" means "cock" and is also said to be a clan name.
Second Division, Volume Three: Mount Aśvakarṇa (*Assakaṇṇa*). It should be called *Iṣādhara*;
it is translated as "Small Fork."
The second fascicle of the Mahīśāsaka-vinaya, translated by Guṇavarman on Mount Mūla;
the sixth fascicle begins with Mount Sumāra, which should be called *Sumāra*.
"Su" means excellent, and "māra" means successive practice.
Volume Fourteen, Gayā Mountain, translated as "The Name of the Country";
Volume Twenty, Parvata Mountain, translated as "Strong";
Volume Twenty, Ahu Mountain, translated as "Sun."
In the thirty-fourth fascicle, *Santiparvata* should be rendered as *Nadīpāṇipāra*;
*nadi* means "house" (*kula*), *pāṇi* means "water," and *pāra* means "protection.
In the first fascicle of the *Sudarsana-vinaya*, *Aśvakarṇa-parvata* is translated as "Earring" (*śruti*).
In the second fascicle: Mount Kṣāraśaila should be called Miśraka;
the translation is "Mixed. Mount Carakācala is translated as "Covered. Mount Cetiya is translated as "Heap. In the third fascicle:
Mount Cetiya is translated as "Awakening. Mount Devakoṭa is translated as "Celestial Terrace. Mount Śūrpakoṭa should be called Śūrpa-khaṭa.
The translation says: "Surname Taikajalaviṣu Mountain" (the translation says: "Surname"); "Śabdusuna" (the translation says: "Sound-Sudana"); "Aśvakarṇa" (it should be called Aśokagallana;
the translation says: "Horse-Ear"); "Īṣādhara Mountain" (it should be called Rīṣigiri); "Rṣigiri" (the translation says: "Seer Mountain").
Volume Eight: Mount Citra, translated as "Various" (zhǒngzhǒng).
Volume Fifteen: Mount Smṛtimat, translated as "Recollection" (niàn).
*The Mahāvaipulya Mahāsannipāta Sūtra*, Volume One: Mount Ṛṣigiri, translated as "Sage" (xiān).
The *Sūtra of the Wise and the Foolish*, Volume Five:
*Mīlūshān* is translated as "Light. The *Lotus Sūtra*, Volume Six: *Mahāmīlūshān* is translated as "Light"; *Yílèluóshān* is translated as "The Abode of the Rishis.
The *Sūtra of One Hundred Parables*, Volume One: *Qílí* is translated as "Mountain."
*Madhyamāgama* (Mātṛkā-sūtra), Volume 8; translated by Anashe as "Place Without Food.
*Buddhanusmṛti-samādhi-sūtra*, Volume 8; translated by Enashan as "Meal," also rendered as "Mother.
*Samantaprabhāsa-sūtra*, Volume 7; *Vaiśālī* should be transcribed as *Pishesheli*.
Translated as:
*The Extensive Propagation of the Sūtra Compiled by Saṃgharakṣa*, Volume Three; translated at Mount Cālika. "Cālika" means "to move. Translated as:
*The Bodhisattva’s Dwelling in the Womb Sūtra*, Volume One; translated at Mount Kaja. "Kaja" means "to ascend."
The *Buddhacarita*, Fascicle II. "Videha" (毘提訶) is translated as "the Land of the Sun. "Paṇḍava" (般荼婆) is translated as "yellow-amaranth color.
The *Sūtra on the Causes and Effects of Past and Present*, Fascicle III. "Cakravāḍa" (遮迦和) is translated as "wheel. The *Pure Candra-sūtra*, lower fascicle.
The *Indraśailaguha-sūtra* refers to it as the "Stone Chamber of the Indra Tree."
The *Sarvabuddhasamāgama-sūtra*, Volume One, translated by Yìzhēnlínduóluó (因眞隣陀羅) at Mount Mùlín;
"Xiǎowáng" (曉王) means King of Dawn.
Volume Two, translated by Mólíshān (摩梨山); "Mólí" (摩梨) refers to the presence of flowers.
In the *Biepin toufa zhong* (Among the Various Vinaya Rules of Piṇḍola), *Vipula Mountain* is translated as "Broken.
In the *Zunzhe qudijia duyi siwei jing* (Sūtra on the Venerable Gautika’s Solitary Contemplation), *Khadira Mountain* is translated as "Sail.
In the *Guankongzang pusa jing* (Sūtra on the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha), *Urumanda Mountain* is translated as "Uru" meaning "Great," and "Manda" meaning "First."
The *Śreṣṭhidāraka-sūtra* refers to Mount Tāṇḍya as "Tāṇḍa," which is translated as "shelter" (*chāyā*).
The *Sūtra of Sutanu* refers to Mount Khararicchi as "Khararicchi," which is translated as "blue."
The *Ākāśagarbha-sūtra*, translated by Achalu Shan, says: "Immovable.
The *Mantra-poison* (Zhudu), translated by Jianamohe Xingshan, says: "Gandha," meaning fragrance.
The *Mahāyāna-mantra-thief-sūtra*, translated by Hemoshan, says: "Gold."
The *Mahādeva-senāpati-mantra-sūtra*, translated at Mount Ārāṭa, says: "Soundless.
The *Tri-laghu-kalpa-uddhṛta-sūtra*, translated at Mount Aśvapa, says: "Without incantations. Regarding Mount Vinata, it should be called Vinatā;
the *Nāḍali-śāstra* states: "Each person has their own mountain."
The *Foguo zhuan* (Records of Foreign Kingdoms), Volume One, in the biography of Pūrṇaśrī, states:
“Mount Lìtóu. Volume Three, in the biography of Śrīmant, states: “The King’s Consort. Volume Four, in the biography of Khaṇḍaśīla, states:

“Rock Mountain. In the biography of Anavaśīra, it states: “Eastern Rock Mountain. In the biography of Avaśīra, it states: “Western Rock Mountain. In the biography of Abhijit, it states: “Wúguǐ Wèi’é Mountain” (Mountain of the Spiritless Wei-é). In the biography of Citragupta, it states: “Lǎo’é Shén Mountain” (Divine Mount Lao-é). In the biography of Maṇicūḍa, it states: “Zhūyù Huànmàn Mountain”; it should instead be called “Huómó.”

translated as "śirīṣa," it has thorns. The *tāla* tree is also called *tāra*;

The translation states: *Nada* means "river"; *Khadira* means "the tree that destroys corpses," also called *Nyagrodha*, translated as "four-branches" or "knotless.
Volume Four: *Bilva* tree; the translator says it is the Bodhisattva tree.
In the twelfth fascicle, *śamālī* tree should be rendered as *śāmbalī*, translated as "cottonwood.
*Ariṣṭa* should be rendered as *hariṣṭa*, translated as "ringless. *Pārijātaka* tree is also called *pārijāta*.
The translation states: *pāri* means "protecting"; *citrataṭa* means "various"; *sāla* is translated as "fir.
In the twenty-third fascicle, *Jambūnada* should be rendered as *Jambunada*;
the translation states: *jambu* refers to the tree, and *nada* means "river."
In the thirtieth fascicle of the *Avataṃsaka-sūtra*, the term *udaka-sāra-candana* appears; *udaka* means "superior" and *sāra* means "essence.
In the forty-ninth fascicle, the *nakṣatra* tree should be called *nakṣatara*, translated as "star";
the *baka* tree is translated as "white heron."
The *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra*, Volume Nine. *Śīkara-vṛkṣa*: translated as "not black" or also as "untimely. *Bālāśa-vṛkṣa*: translated as "red flower.
*Karṇikāra-vṛkṣa*: should be called *cañcarīka*; translated as "ear-cut. *Aśoka-vṛkṣa*: should be called *aśoka*; translated as "sorrowless. *Pāṭala-vṛkṣa*:
translated as "heavy. *Rocana*: translated as "cow bezoar. *Āmra-vṛkṣa*: should be called *āmrapāla*; also called *āmra*.
Translated as "The Sour Fruit," Volume Twenty-Six; translated by Sanghavarman as "Tilling the Fields," Volume Twenty-Seven;
regarding the *udumbara* tree, it should be called *utpala*.
The translation states: *U* means "to arise"; *tambala* means "emptiness. Volume thirty:
*kṣemara* should be called *kṣemadruma*;
the translation states: "fragrant flowers."
*Ekottarika Āgama*, fascicle 29, translated by Mòluó (末羅), states: "Surname" (*xing*) may also be called "Power" (*lì*).
*Dīrgha Āgama*, fascicle 3, *Pāṭaligāma*: it should be read as *Pāṭaligāma*.

Translated, *pāṭali* means "flower" and *gāma* is as explained above. *Campā*: translated as "golden flower tree. *Pāpā*: translated as "Pāpā" [the place] where people "delight" (*lè*). *Rammaka*: translated as "good joy. *Vāsabhagāma*: translated as "summer-born. *Gayā*: the translator says this is the name of a country. *Bhaddasāla*: it should be read as *Bhaddasāla*; in Chinese it is called *báduō ānluó* (跋陀安羅).
Translated as: *Bhara* means "virtuous," and *śāra* means "substance.
The second fascicle of the *Saṃyukta Āgama*. *Pāriyātra-kovidāra* tree; translated as: *pāriyātra* means "excellent play," and *kovidāra* means "earth-breaker.
Fascicle nineteen. *Bharaviṣa*; translated as "Great Entry."
In the sixth fascicle of the *Daśabhāṇavāra-vinaya*,
the seventh section on the "Seven Dharmas," the term *śīra* should be translated as "stone" (*śīla*), and the term *kapittha* should be translated as "pear" (*kapittha*).
In the thirty-third fascicle of the *Mahāsāṃghika-vinaya*, translated by Ālidu Jiāng, "āriṭa" is translated as "yellow ginger.
In the ninth fascicle of the *Dharmaguptaka-vinaya*, translated by Jiàntuoshù, "kharjūra" is translated as "earth-holding," and "harītakī" is translated as "heavenly-holder.
In the twelfth fascicle of the *Mahīśāsaka-vinaya*, "āmalaka" is translated as "stainless," "vibhītaka" is translated as "fearless," and "ilā-vṛkṣa" is translated as "fragrant."
Volume 19: *Mātṛ* is translated as "to examine. Volume 31:
*Vagha-pa* should be called *Bhāgava*;
the translator states this is a clan name (*gotra*).
The *Sudarsana-vinaya-vibhāṣā*, Scroll One, translated by Luo Da: "Śveta" (勝馬) means "Victorious Horse. *Khadirāmravṛkṣa* (楗陀菴羅樹): "Fragrant Fruit Tree. Scroll Three:
*Mandāravṛkṣa* (蔓陀羅律): "Refined Tree. Scroll Four: *Mahāśālipa-vṛkṣa* (摩訶沙利波樹):
"Mahāli" means "Great," "Śāli" means "Rice," and "Pa" means "Possession"; thus it is the "Great Rice Tree. *Panasavṛkṣa* (波那沙樹): "Great Fruit Tree."
Volume 14: *Mukhara* translated as "Victory" (*jaya*).
Volume 17: *Bharahi* translated as "Cloud. *Śama* translated as "Tranquility. *Citrāpāṭalī* tree: *Citrā* means "various," and *Pāṭalī* means "double-flowered.
*Abhidharma-vibhāṣā*, Volume 7: *Vatsiputra* translated by Luo as "Victory."
Volume Twelve: *Rohiṇī-bhaiṣajya-ādi*; the translator states: "It resembles a lotus. Volume Fourteen:
*Pāṭala-vṛkṣa*; translated as: "The Great [Tree].
Volume Seventeen: *Kañcana-vana*; translated as: "Gold."
Volume Twenty-Seven: *Satyaka-jñāma* should be rendered as *Satyanī-ma*. Translated:
*Satya* means "truth" (*satya*), and it is also called "reality" (*ṛta*). *Jñāma* means "vow" (*pratijñā*) or "commitment. *Citrataḍa* should be rendered as *Citrataḍa*. Translated:
*Citratā* means "various," and *taḍa* means "unpleasant" (*apriya*). *Mikṣika-vana* is translated as "Miscellaneous Grove" (*Miśraka-vana*). *Nandana* should be rendered as *Nanda-vana*.
The translation says: "Forest of Joy" (*Nandanavana*). *Sahasra* should be translated as *nagara*, which means "good.
*Vibhāṣā* in two fascicles; *Kapiñjala* should be translated as *Kapiñjala*.
The translation says: *kūta* means "bird"; *īṣat* means "joy"; *nālikāra* means "leakage"; *vṛkṣa* means "tree"; *māluka* means "upright.
In the third fascicle of the *Chuyao jing* (Udānavarga), *sālu* means "good tree";
in the ninth fascicle, *karana* means "making."
*The Flower-Peak Sūtra*, Scroll Five, translated by Juelu Shu; titled "Garden and Grove.
*The Ten Abodes and Severing of Bonds*, Scroll Seven, translated by Jingyi Jinfan Shengqu Shu; titled "Myna Bird.
*The Vāsumitra Sūtra*, Scroll Three, translated by Chashouli Shu; titled "Sparrow."
*The Sūtra of One Hundred Parables*, Volume One. Translated by Pózhāshù. The translator notes that it resembles the *bodhi* tree.
Volume Four mentions the *póhuán* tree; it should be called *xún pó pō nà*, translated as "the fine tree."
The *Dù wújí jīng* (Sutra on the Perfection of Crossing Over), Volume 8, translated by Yingjiata;
titled *Tǐ yǔ guān fó sānmèi jīng* (Sutra on the Body and the Samādhi of Contemplating the Buddha), Volume 1, translated by Bōtuóluó; titled *Pò* (Break);
the *Xiánjié jīng* (Sutra of the Worthy Kalpa), Volume 3, translated by Shìshéhé; *Shù* should be rendered as *Shēngshèpó*.
Translated as: *Śirīṣa*, the son of Rāma; translated as: "Play. *Pāṭalī* flower tree; translated as: "Delivering Beings" (Sukhāvatīvyūha).
*Nianfo Sanmei Jing* (Sutra on the Samādhi of Recollecting the Buddha), Volume One. *Tāla* flower tree; translated as: "Rolling/Whirling. *Kadamba* flower tree; translated as:
"White Flower. Volume Four. *Kakudha* tree; it should be called *Kakubha*.
Translated as:
"The Collection of Saṃgharakṣa," Fascicle Two. Regarding "Kāśyapa-vāṭa," it should be rendered as "Kāpiśī-vāṭa.
The translator states: "Kāpiśī" is the name of a rishi; "vāṭa" refers to his dwelling place.
*Yizu jing*, lower fascicle; *Suweitu shu*: should be called *Susacani*.
Translated as "Fine Pavilion.
Two fascicles. *Niepan jing*, first fascicle; *Dimiluo shu*: translated as "Subtle."
*The Biography of Akṣobhya*, Scroll Lower. Regarding the *āmlī* tree (*āmlapatra*), it should be called *aśvattha*;
translated, *aśva* means "horse" and *patra* means "foot. Regarding the *laṃbī* tree, it is translated as "hanging.

In the ninth volume of the *Fan-yu* (Translation of Sanskrit Terms), the original text states: "On the tenth day of the late spring in the second year of the Nintei era, this was completed at the eastern shelter of Jizō-in in Teirō-ji, for the flourishing of the Buddha-dharma. Recorded by the junior student of the Esoteric School, the Shamon Shinken of Tō-ji."
Fanyan yu, Scroll Ten:
Names of Grasses, Number Sixty-three;
Names of Fragrances, Number Sixty-four.
[Signature] The *Daosheng tong* (Compendium of the Path) was completed on the tenth day of the fourth month at the southern side of the same monastery.

Shenyuan (right), having obtained a copy of the text transmitted by Master Shenxian of Dizang Monastery, recorded his labor in proofreading it and had it deposited in the sutra repository of Guanzhi Monastery. Completed on the twenty-eighth day of the eighth month of the first year of Kwanpō, the Xin-you year. Sengzheng Xianhe, fifty-eight years of age.
